slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single copy occupying the whole 512-byte EEPROM. Valid iff RAM-order magic at struct+0 is 'driv' (file offset 4, block-reversed 'vird') and u32 LE sum8 at struct+4 (file offset 0, block-reversed) equals the byte sum of struct[8:512). FUN_08778000 retries the 64-block read 4 times, then writes the magic and zeroes struct[4:512) in RAM. No backup copy, no generation counter.

checksums.name: header_sum8_504
checksums.formula_detail: stored_u32le(RAM struct+4) == sum of unsigned bytes RAM struct[8:512) (504 bytes, 0x1F8), accumulated in a 32-bit int with no seed/complement. File image is the RAM image with each 8-byte block byte-reversed, so the stored field appears at file offset 0 as 00 00 02 f0 and the covered byte multiset at file[8:512) is identical. Decompiled proof: FUN_08778000 sums 0x1F8 bytes from _DAT_087780c0+8 and compares with _DAT_087780c0[1].

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive: programs DMA source/dest/count (count|0x80000000 enable) via unresolved _DAT_ register symbols, busy-waits on control bit 0x8000. Used for both EEPROM command write and data read DMA.

EEPROM 8-byte block read (MMIO seed, sole 0x0D000000 user). Builds read command (two leading 1 bits + address bits), DMA-writes addr_bits+3 cells, DMA-reads 0x44 cells, re-packs 4 halfwords MSB-first to descending RAM addresses. Caller edge from decompiled body of FUN_08778000 (alias func_0x08778848); missing in callgraph.json.
EEPROM/DMA configuration select called with argument 4 before each load attempt; branches on 4 vs 0x40 vs other to write different config globals (SDK EEPROM size/address-width setup).

Load+validate+checksum+blank-init: reads 0x40 blocks (512 B) into RAM struct at _DAT_087780c0, checks magic, sums 504 bytes, retries 4 times, else writes magic and zeroes 508 bytes at struct+4. No EEPROM write performed here.

Default profile-record initializer (orphan, no traced caller): writes u32 'save' constant, 'A', spaces, 0x20, 0x80, then zeroes the record. Destination mapped to struct+0x80 by byte-exact match with both .sav files.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot/save load: configure EEPROM (arg 4), read 64 blocks of 8 bytes via DMA3 to/from 0x0D000000, validate magic+sum8, retry x4, else fabricate blank struct in RAM.
ram_fields_updated: whole 512-byte struct filled by block reads
caller_chains.how_mapped: Decompiled bodies in ghidra/decompiled.c; callgraph.json corroborates 0x08778848->0x087787c8. FUN_08778000 calls FUN_08778848 via unresolved alias func_0x08778848 (64-iteration loop), so that edge is absent from callgraph.json and FUN_08778000 is absent from its keys.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Default/new profile creation (caller not traced). Writes the default record that appears at struct+0x80 in both samples.
caller_chains.how_mapped: No call edge exists in callgraph.json or decompiled.c. Mapped by byte-pattern identity: every non-zero write of FUN_0800289c (u32 const, 0x41, 0x20 x3, 0x20, 0x80, zero runs) reproduces the observed RAM-reversed bytes at file 0x80..0x90 in order, fixing the u32 constant as 'save' (0x65766173 LE) and the destination as struct+0x80.

fields.name: stored_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: Recompute sum8 over RAM struct[8:512), store u32 LE at struct+4, block-reverse each 8-byte block into the file. FUN_08778000 zeroes this field on the blank-init path (sum of zeroed payload is 0, self-consistent). The EEPROM flush writer that persists it is not in the corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_08778000: sums 0x1F8 bytes from struct+8, compares with u32 at struct+4. Python: sav-01 full-range computed 0x2f0 == stored; sav-00 prefix [8:0x90) computed 0x2f0 == stored, full range 0x17180 due to erased 0xFF tail. File offset 0 is the block-reversed image of RAM struct+4.

fields.name: magic_driv
fields.update_mechanism: Constant u32 LE 0x76697264 ('driv') at RAM struct+0; FUN_08778000 compares it against iRam087780c4 before the checksum and rewrites it on the blank-init path. Never changes in a valid save.
fields.evidence: FUN_08778000 magic gate and rewrite; ASCII 'driv' appears in both files only under the verified 8-byte block reversal (file 'vird' at offset 4). RAM mirror struct+0x00 (absolute base _DAT_087780c0 unresolved).

fields.name: reserved_zero_008_07f
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed by FUN_08778000 blank-init path; included in the checksum range. No other writer/reader in the corpus addresses individual bytes here.
fields.evidence: Inside both the summed range [8:512) and the zeroed range [4:512) in FUN_08778000; all-zero in both .sav files. RAM struct+0x08..+0x80. Semantics unknown; reserved.

fields.name: profile_name
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_0800289c writes u32 'save' (0x65766173 LE) then bytes 0x41 'A', 0x20, 0x20, 0x20 at record+0..+8. Space-padded 8-char name, written at default/profile creation; modifying it requires checksum repair.
fields.evidence: Byte-exact match between FUN_0800289c's non-zero write sequence and RAM-reversed file bytes at 0x80 in both files. RAM struct+0x80..+0x88. No reader in corpus (menu code not traced).

fields.name: profile_byte_088
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_0800289c writes 0x20 at record+8. File offset 143 (0x8F) is its position after 8-byte block reversal of the block starting at file 0x88.
fields.evidence: Initializer write *(param_1+2)=0x20 at byte +8 reproduced in both .sav files under block reversal. RAM struct+0x88. Meaning unknown.

fields.name: profile_flag_089
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_0800289c writes 0x80 at record+9 (also mirrored to a global). File offset 142 (0x8E) after block reversal. Changing it requires checksum repair.
fields.evidence: Initializer byte +9 = 0x80 matches observed byte in both files; no reader in the corpus proves flag semantics, so bitflags typing is structural only. RAM struct+0x89.

fields.name: profile_record_tail_zero
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed by FUN_0800289c's zero runs (record+0x0A onward) and by FUN_08778000 blank-init; included in checksum.
fields.evidence: File bytes 0x88..0x8D are zero in both files (the two non-zero bytes of this 8-byte block sit at file 0x8E/0x8F, i.e. RAM struct+0x89/+0x88 after block reversal). Zeroed by FUN_0800289c record+0x0A onward and FUN_08778000 blank-init; inside checksum range.

fields.name: unused_tail_090_1ff
fields.update_mechanism: Read and summed by FUN_08778000 (64-block read reaches struct+0x200 exactly); zeroed in RAM on the blank-init path. EEPROM flush writer not in corpus, so the 0xFF->0x00 transition between snapshots cannot be attributed to a specific function.
fields.evidence: Sole inter-snapshot delta per saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt (368 bytes at 0x90..0x200). Inside checksum range [8:512); explains sav-00 full-range sum mismatch (0x17180 vs stored 0x2f0). RAM struct+0x90..+0x200.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Alter one byte of the block-reversed magic (RAM 'driv' -> 'driw') with no checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08778000 magic gate fails; after retries the RAM struct is reinitialised (magic rewritten, rest zeroed) and the profile is lost on reload. Confirms magic gate and absence of a backup copy.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Increment the stored checksum (RAM u32 752 -> 753) with no other change
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Magic passes, sum mismatches, same reinitialisation as the magic mutation. Distinguishes the checksum gate from the magic gate.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change RAM profile name 'saveA   ' -> 'testB   ' (edit in RAM order, re-reverse blocks)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save accepted; profile/menu display or reloaded RAM name shows 'testB'. If display unchanged, the name is re-derived at load and the field is cosmetic.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip profile flag byte RAM+0x89 (file 0x8E) 0x80 -> 0x00, then 0x80 -> 0x81 in a second run
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Any profile present/locked/state change identifies the bit's role; no change in either run indicates a constant marker rather than a flag.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set RAM+0x08 = 0x01, once without and once with checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Without repair: reinitialisation (empirically proves reserved region is summed). With repair: acceptance with no visible change proves the byte unused; any gameplay/UI delta reveals a hidden field at +0x08. Sweep +0x08/+0x40/+0x7F to map the reserved region.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set RAM+0x1FF (last covered byte; file block at 0x1F8) = 0x01 on the zero-tail sav-01 image with repair; repeat on the 0xFF-tail sav-00 image without touching the tail
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Acceptance on sav-01 proves coverage reaches +0x200. On sav-00, rejection proves the game sums the on-disk 0xFF tail; acceptance proves it sums only a zeroed RAM tail — resolving the sav-00 checksum anomaly.

open_questions: EEPROM flush writer absent: no EEPROM write-opcode builder, no second 0x0D000000 user, no SRAM (0x0E000000) or Flash (0x5555/0x2AAA) path exists among the 85 decompiled functions. Which function persists the RAM struct, when does it run, and does it write all 64 blocks or only dirty ones?
Absolute RAM base of the save struct (_DAT_087780c0 in FUN_08778000) is an unresolved Ghidra pointer; only struct-relative offsets are known, so ram_addr is null throughout.

Caller of FUN_0800289c (default profile initializer) is untraced; its destination struct+0x80 is mapped by byte-pattern identity, not by a call edge. What menu/boot path calls it and with what base pointer?

sav-00 tail (0x90..0x200) is erased 0xFF while sav-01 is 0x00 with identical active bytes and an identical stored checksum (752, matching a zero tail). Was the tail flushed between frames 1119 and 1157, or is the difference emulator backing-store fill? Fuzzing target at offset 504 is designed to decide this.

Semantics of profile bytes RAM+0x88 (0x20) and RAM+0x89 (0x80) and of any future fields in the reserved (0x08..0x80) and tail (0x90..0x200) regions are unknown: only one profile state (default 'saveA') exists in the corpus, so no differential mapping is possible.

FUN_08778780 configuration semantics (argument 4 vs 0x40 profiles) and the unresolved DMA register symbols (_DAT_08778828..08778844) prevent quoting exact DMA3 register addresses beyond the 0x0D000000 EEPROM window literal.
callgraph.json omits FUN_08778000 entirely and lacks the FUN_08778000 -> FUN_08778848 edge (unresolved alias); graph coverage of the boot path is incomplete relative to the decompiled bodies.
